# XCP protocol discipline

Tethys is a clean-room implementation of ASAM XCP 1.4 (S1 in `docs/research/phase-0-system-requirements.md`). Every line of protocol code traces to a spec section so reviewers can verify conformance.

## Required citation patterns

In the C / Python file header that hosts protocol logic:

```c
/* XCP 1.4 §1.3.2.4 CONNECT command - see docs/research/phase-0-system-requirements.md §4 */
```

In the commit body (Conventional Commits style):

```text
feat(slave): implement CONNECT command per XCP 1.4 §1.3.2.4

Cite: ASAM XCP 1.4 Part 2 §1.3.2.4
Trace: docs/traceability.csv row XCP-CMD-CONNECT
```

## Banned patterns

- Implementing a protocol command without a `§` citation in the file header.
- Silently diverging from the XCP wire format. If the spec is ambiguous, file a Research-Note issue and document in `docs/research/phase-N-protocol-clarification.md`.
- Citing the Vector XCP Book (S3) as the normative source - it is a *reference*, the normative source is ASAM MCD-1 XCP 1.4.

## Recovery + extension

XCP itself does not retransmit DAQ (§4.2 of the system-requirements note). When implementing recovery semantics, cite both the XCP base spec and `docs/adr/drafts/adr-0010-packet-loss-tolerance-budget.md`.

## Verification

PR-4 `p0-ci` adds a workflow that greps every `slave/src/core/**.c` and `master/src/tethys_master/protocol/**.py` file for at least one `XCP 1.4 §` citation; CI fails if absent.
